part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `do_write_float` (include/fmt/format.h:2649), in the `1234e-2 -> 12.34` branch: when computing the padded width for localized output, it called `grouping.count_separators(significand_size)`, counting thousands separators over the *entire* significand including fractional digits. But `write_significand` only applies grouping to the integral part (`exp` digits), so the computed size exceeded the actual content by the number of phantom separators — underfilling the padded width by that amount (e.g. `1.295` counted a separator for the "1295" significand that never appears in "1.295").

The fix counts separators over the integral part only: `count_separators(exp)`.

Verified with a reproduction using a `numpunct` facet with 3-digit grouping: all `{:19.3Lf}` outputs are now width 19 and match their non-localized widths, and the full test suite passes (format-test, xchar-test/locale tests, core-test, format-impl-test, printf-test, chrono-test, ranges-test, etc.).
